## On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503s

**Status:** Ongoing as of end of log coverage (03:59:27Z) — pool backlog still growing, not self-healing.

**Root cause:**
Deploy `dep-4471` (gateway, a.novak, 02:12–02:14Z) — *"config: connection-per-request for pool isolation"* — shipped a config change (generation 118→119, applied 02:13:41.234Z) that flipped `gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true`. Against a fixed pool size of 20, allocating one connection per request exhausts the pool almost immediately under normal traffic.

**Impact window:**
- **Start:** 2026-03-14 02:14:18.972Z (first `503`, req-07401), ~38s after the config applied.
- **End:** none — still active at last log entry, 03:59:27.974Z. Queue depth (`waiting`) climbed steadily from 18 to 74 over that period with no recovery.
- **Scope:** gateway only. Routes hit: `/v1/cart`, `/v1/session`, `/v1/catalog/search`, `/v1/orders`, `/v1/checkout` (all backends: catalog-svc, orders-svc, accounts-svc, billing-svc). `/health` kept returning 200 throughout, so this wasn't caught by basic health checks. Confirmed via `logs/worker.log` that the worker fleet (job runner) was unaffected — no errors, no elevated db_wait, unrelated to this incident.

**Error signature:** every 503 paired with `ERROR pool ... ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting N)`, preceded by `WARN pool ... acquire slow` as an early indicator (first at 02:14:14.920Z).

**Action: roll back `dep-4471`** — revert `gateway.pool.perRequest` to `false` (or push a new config generation restoring it). No other deploy in the window is implicated (`dep-4470` worker deploy finished 00:55Z, well before; `dep-4472` billing-svc deploy didn't start until 02:41Z, after the outage was already underway).
